title: The Sleeping Greenhouse
theme: A hundred years asleep, and a thorny vine has sealed the only door.
description: Wake a fern, bribe a biting cactus, and read a gardener's poem to set a stone guardian's symbol rings.
intro: The greenhouse fell asleep a hundred years ago, and so did everything in it. Moonlight drips through cracked glass. A thorny vine has sealed the door, and a mossy stone guardian stands watch over it, holding three rings of carved symbols.

clues.poem: Scratched into the potting bench: "First the bloom that drinks the moon, then the jaws that snap at noon, last the fern that sleeps in tune."
clues.moonSymbol: The moonflower's centre is etched with ☾.
clues.sunSymbol: Carved into the snapjaw cactus's pot: ☀.

inspect.title: The door
say: The withered vines crumble to dust as you push, and the door swings open onto a garden full of fireflies.

inspect.title: The door
say: Thorny vines have grown across the door, thick as rope. They tighten when you touch them, and the stone guardian's eyes follow your hand.
A moonflower, the only thing here wide awake, glowing softly. Etched in its centre: ☾. A single honey drop trembles on one petal.
The moonflower glows softly, drinking the moonlight. Etched in its centre: ☾.
A barrel brimming with rainwater. The moon floats on its surface like a coin someone dropped.
You dip the can. The rainwater comes up shimmering silver, as if you'd scooped up a little of the moon.
The can is already full to the brim.
The fern has unfurled, stretching and yawning. Hidden in its fronds is a symbol of a flower: ✿.
A fern curled into a tight green fist, fast asleep. Something is hidden deep in its fronds, out of reach.
You water the fern with moonwater. It shivers, uncurls, and yawns, revealing a symbol hidden in its fronds: ✿.
The can is empty. The fern doesn't even stir.
A potting bench buried in soil and seed packets. A poem is scratched into the wood: "First the bloom that drinks the moon, then the jaws that snap at noon, last the fern that sleeps in tune."
A battered watering can sits on top.
Scratched into the wood: "First the bloom that drinks the moon, then the jaws that snap at noon, last the fern that sleeps in tune."
The snapjaw cactus is purring, its belly full of honey. Carved into its pot: ☀.
A cactus with a mouth full of thorns. It snaps at your fingers before you can see what's carved into its pot.
You toss the honey drop. The cactus gulps it down, purrs, and lolls aside, revealing a symbol carved into its pot: ☀.
The cactus slurps the water and snaps at you anyway. Water isn't what it wants.
The stone guardian has lowered its arms. Its job is done.
A moss-covered stone guardian holds three rings of carved symbols. Its stone eyes are fixed on the vine-covered door.

lock.title: The stone guardian
lock.prompt: Turn the three rings of symbols.

solved.title: The stone guardian
say: The rings grind into place: ☾ ☀ ✿. The guardian lowers its arms, and with a long, dry hiss the vines across the door wither and fall away.

wrong: The rings grind and slip back. The guardian does not move.
A low rumble of stone. Wrong symbols, or the wrong order.
Moss sprinkles down. The guardian waits.

levels: The potting bench has something to read and something to carry.
Inspect the potting bench: read the poem and take the watering can.
The sleeping fern needs waking. What do plants love?
An empty can won't help. Where could you fill it?
Fill the watering can at the rain barrel, then use it on the sleeping fern.
The snapjaw cactus is hiding something, but it bites.
Something sweet might calm it. The moonflower is holding something.
Take the honey drop from the moonflower and give it to the snapjaw cactus.
Each plant shows a symbol, and the poem gives an order.
Match each line of the poem to a plant: the bloom that drinks the moon, the jaws that snap, the fern that sleeps.
Moonflower ☾, snapjaw cactus ☀, fern ✿. Set the guardian's rings to ☾ ☀ ✿.
Click the door to leave the greenhouse.

wrongItemLine: A leaf shakes its head at you. That doesn't belong there.
escapeText: The last vine crumbles, the door swings open on a garden full of fireflies, and behind you a hundred sleeping plants stir and turn their faces to the moon.
